reason: The rover needs a pen, so I'll start by fitting it into the clip.
expectation: I expect a pen held in its clip, ready to attach to the rover.

alternatives.reason: Powering the remote also looks necessary, but I'll prepare the drawing tool first.

effect: The pen is clipped and ready to fit to the rover.
reason: Attaching the clipped pen should give the rover its drawing tool.
expectation: I expect the pen to be mounted on the rover, though it may still need adjustment.

alternatives.reason: The remote also needs power, but I'll finish mounting the pen first.

effect: The pen is mounted; the remote is the next available preparation.
reason: Powering the remote is the only offered combination and should enable steering.
expectation: I expect a powered remote, ready to control the rover.

effect: The remote now has power and is ready to use with the rover.
reason: Using the remote with the rover is the only offered combination and should let me test its steering.
expectation: I expect the remote to control the rover, though the pen may still need adjustment.

effect: The steering test revealed unequal motor speeds and a trim adjustment to correct them.
reaction: The curve makes the need for adjustment clear.
reason: The screwdriver is the only offered combination and should adjust the motor trim.
expectation: I expect to adjust the trim so the rover travels straighter, though it may need another test.

effect: The trim balances the wheel speeds, so the rover is ready for another drawing test.
reaction: Adjusting the control rather than the drawing makes the correction clear.
reason: The test paper is the only offered combination and should let me try the trimmed rover.
expectation: I expect to test whether the rover now draws a straighter line.

effect: The test confirms the trim produces a straight line, and different wheel speeds steer the rover into a loop.
reaction: Seeing the steering principle make a visible mark is satisfying.
reason: The pen-lift lever is the only offered combination and should let the rover move without drawing.
expectation: I expect the lever to lift the pen off the paper so the rover can travel without leaving a line.

effect: The pen-lift lever is fitted, ready to test with the remote.
reason: Using the remote is the only offered combination and should test the completed rover.
expectation: I expect to steer the rover and try moving with the pen lifted, though I don't know exactly how the test will unfold.

effect: The final test confirms the rover can move without marking, then draw a whale for the invitation; the chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The looping whale is a pleasing payoff for the pen lift.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the trimmed rover was most worthwhile: the straight line and loop made the relationship between wheel speeds and steering visible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Powering the remote was a necessary but unremarkable preparation.

surprise.text: The initial straight-ahead command produced a curve because one motor was faster; the trim corrected the control rather than the drawing.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary, although several fittings were straightforward and offered as the only choice.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the drawing rover and the whale invitation fit into the fair, especially if another mechanism is demonstrated as clearly as the steering.
